newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAISES HIGHER EDUCATION BUDGET 11.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAISES HIGHER EDUCATION BUDGET 11.2 PCT.

text.p: The South African government has upped the 1997/98 budget allocation for tertiary education by 11.2 percent to 4.8 billion rand, Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu said on Thursday.

Bengu told a news conference the increase, slightly above the average 1996 inflation rate of 9.4 percent, was agreed to by the cabinet not because of countrywide campus protests about the cost of higher education.
He added, however, that because of increased student numbers, the average funding level would drop from 68 percent of total operating cost to 65.6 percent.
"Some institutions will get a little above the average and others a little below, but the national average will be 65.59 percent," he said.

Bengu said the government would not finalise plans to thin out the total of 36 universities and technikons, which offer diploma level training, until a policy white paper on higher education was finalised later this year.

He said South Africa had 176,000 students at 15 technikons and 234,000 students at 21 universities, adding he would like to see the ratios reversed with more students studying technical and practical subjects than at university.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's March 12 budget for fiscal 1997/98 will for the first time not include specific allocations for school spending.

Instead, Manuel will allocate block amounts to the nine provinces, expected to account for about 60 percent of government expenditure, and local governments will determine the share for schools and other purposes.
Apart from a deficit for borrowing of four percent, Bengu's higher education allocation is one of the first firm budget figures to be made public.
